sentences.text: .... Resp  Date of receiving of Appeal : 22.12.2015  Date of arguments : 11.05.2016  Date of judgment : 14.05.2016  JUDGMENT 1

By this judgment I will dispose of appeal u/sec.374 Cr.PC. filed on behalf of convict M/s Kadimi Sweets against the judgment dated 17.09.2015 and order on sentence dated 19.09.2015 passed by Sh. Gaurav Rao, Ld. ACMM-II, Patiala House Court, New Delhi.
2 The brief facts of the case as per record and from trial court record are that accused is an establishment namely M/s Kadimi Sweets Pvt. Ltd. at C-5A Market, Janakpuri, New Delhi-58.

On 20.11.2002 at about 2.30 p.m. Food Inspector Sh. V. P. S. Chaudhary visited the said CA No. 96/15 M/s Kadimi Sweets Vs. State page 1 of 6 place and purchased 1500 grams of " Laddoo Motichoor"
from accused.

entities.text: CA No. 96/15 M/s Kadimi Sweets Vs. State
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: FI was accompanied with SDM/LHA Sh. M. A. Ashraf.
The said Laddoo Motichoor was purchased for the purposes of analysis under PFA Act.
The same sample was divided into three parts, packed as per Rules of PFA.
Panchanama was prepared.
One sample was sent for analysis to Public Analyst.
During investigation, it was found that the said establishment has appointed Sh. Mansa Ram as its nominee under PFA Act.

As per the report of Analyst, sample did not confirm to the standard because "The sample is adulterated because Total dye content of synthetic colour used exceeds the prescribed maximum limit of 100 PPM (428.59 PPM)."

sentences.text: 1 3 As the sample was failed, prosecution was launched by Food Inspector by filing complaint dated 28.03.2003 with the court.
Accused was summoned.
He has exercised his right u/sec.13(2) PFA Act to get the sample analyzed by CFL.

CFL reported "I am of the opinion that the above sample contravenes Rule 30 of the PFA (Tartrazine 335.0 PPM Sunset Yellow FCF 25.0 PPM Total dye 360.0 PMM).
4

Charges were framed against accused company as well as nominee Mansa Ram u/sec.2(ia) (a) (j)
(m) read with sec.7 of PFA Act, 1954 punishable u/sec.16(1A) of PFA Act.

5 After trial, vide judgment dated 17.09.2015 accused was convicted for offence u/sec.16(1A) of PFA Act and vide order on sentence dated 19.09.2015 accused company was fined for Rs.3 lacs while accused Mansa Ram was directed to undergo simple imprisonment for a period of 4 years and two days and fine of Rs.25,000/- and in default of payment of CA No. 96/15 M/s Kadimi Sweets Vs.
State page 2 of 6 fine accused Mansa Ram was directed to undergo SI of 60 days.
He remained in custody for two days.

6 In this appeal, the accused has assailed the judgment on the following grounds:-
(i) Non-compliance of Sec.10(7) of PFA Act and Rule i.e. independent witnesses were not joined (argued orally though not in grounds of appeal).
(ii) There is variation in different reports (PA and CFL) so the sample was not properly homogenized.

(iii) Non-compliance of Rule 14 of PFA Rules i.e. the bottles, spoon, tray etc., were not made clean and dried at the spot by the food inspector or any other official.
(iv) Excessive fine beyond the purview of PFA Act and beyond the jurisdiction of trial court.
7
No reply was filed by respondent/state and the matter was argued orally.
8 I have gone through the record, Trial Court record and have heard the submissions of Ld. counsel for appellant and Ld. SPP for State.
It is argued by counsel for appellant that no public witness was present in the proceedings nor efforts were made to join any public witnesses.
As far as this argument is concerned, the same argument was raised before the Ld. Trial Court.
The same was dealt by the trial court from para 18 to 24 of the judgment.

As far as opinion/finding of the trial court regarding this argument is concerned, I do not find any infirmity in those findings and the same are upheld and the arguments regarding this fact does not find any force and thus rejected.
CA No. 96/15 M/s Kadimi Sweets Vs. State page 3 of 6 9
It is further stated that there is variation in the report of PA and CFL and due to that reason benefit goes in favour of the accused.
This line of argument was done before the trial court and was dealt in para 44 to 90 of the judgment.
I do not want to differ from the reasoning given by the trial court and thus the same is upheld.

M/S Kadimi Sweets Pvt. Ltd vs Food Inspector on 14 May, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/78356086/
2 10

entities.text: Kadimi Sweets Pvt. Ltd vs Food Inspector on 14 May, 2016 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is further argued that compliance u/sec.14 PFA Rules was not proved on record by the prosecution.
It is stated that witnesses are deposing differently with respect to the cleanliness of spoon etc.
It is further stated that it was the duty of the prosecution to prove these facts.
These arguments were also addressed before the trial court.
The relevant part of the judgment dealing with these arguments are from para 25 to 43 of the judgment.
11 As far as the arguments in this regard is concerned, the law discussed by the trial court is correct and the same is self explanatory.
However, as far as the analysis of facts are concerned, to my opinion, the same requires some more elaboration.
12 As far as Rule 14 of PFA Rules are concerned, it spells out that the FI shall use dry bottles or containers for the purposes of sampling.

However, this fact was elaborated further by Hon. Supreme Court in Varghese Vs. Food, 1989 (II) Prevention of Food Adulteration Cases, 236 stating that "it must be the endeavour of the FI to use clean and dry implements in sampling the articles of food.

entities.text: Varghese Vs. Food, 1989 (II) Prevention of Food Adulteration Cases, 236
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If unhygienic methods are adopted, it will effect the result of analysis.
So, the Hon. Supreme Court use the word "implements" instead of only "dry and clean bottles/containers".

Similarly, in other judgments, i.e. State of Haryana Vs. CA No. 96/15 M/s Kadimi Sweets Vs. State page 4 of 6 Kishan Kumar CLT 559, it was observed that the prosecution had not stated that the "weighing scale" was clean.

entities.text: State of Haryana Vs. CA No. 96/15 M/s Kadimi Sweets Vs. State
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Similarly, in other judgments, like Sardar Mal Jain, 1996 (2) Prevention of Food Adulteration Cases, 203, it was stated that the newspaper on which the Barfi was weighed was not clean.

entities.text: Sardar Mal Jain, 1996 (2) Prevention of Food Adulteration Cases, 203
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Similarly, in Shashi Kant Vs. State of UP, 1983 (1) Prevention of Food Adulteration Cases 90, it was observed that the "bhagona" was not proved to be clean and dry.

entities.text: Shashi Kant Vs. State of UP, 1983 (1) Prevention of Food Adulteration Cases 90
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 13 So, accordingly, it can be said that the law which can be crystallized from various judgments of Hon. High Courts as well as Hon. Supreme Court is that if in evidence, the prosecution states that the sample commodity had touched a surface of an "implement" or any other surface, it is the duty of the prosecution to prove beyond reasonable doubt that the said implement/surface was clean and dry and thus could not have added any impurity to the sample.
However, it is not the law that the FI shall spell out on which surfaces the sample commodity had touched while sampling.
However, if he chooses to spell out the implements/surfaces with which the sample commodity came into contact/touch, the same must be proved as clean and dry.
14 In the present case, PW1/FI had deposed in his examination- in-chief that before putting the Laddoos in bottles, the same were broken on a tray.
However, in his cross-examination he had stated that the said tray was provided by the vendor himself.
Similarly, PW2 also deposed that the "spoon and the tray were provided by the accused in which the sample was mixed."

So, from this testimony it can be safely said that after the FI had chosen the Laddoos as sample commodity, the same were broken on CA No. 96/15 M/s Kadimi Sweets Vs. State page 5 of 6 a tray provided by the vendor.

entities.text: CA No. 96/15 M/s Kadimi Sweets Vs. State
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Nowhere it is deposed that the said tray was clean and dry and free from any colour.
15 Hence, proper compliance u/sec.14 PFA Act/Rules is not done.

M/S Kadimi Sweets Pvt. Ltd vs Food Inspector on 14 May, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/78356086/
3 16

entities.text: Kadimi Sweets Pvt. Ltd vs Food Inspector on 14 May, 2016 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: So, in these circumstances, the prosecution failed to prove the strict compliance u/sec.14 of PFA Rules.
17 So, the judgment and order on sentence of the trial court is reversed.

18 Accused M/s Kadimi Sweets Pvt. Ltd. is acquitted of the charges u/sec.16(1A) read with sec.7 of PFA Act.
19 TCR be sent back with copy of the order.
20
File of appeal be consigned to Record Room.
